title: Marble or dice on a tilting tray: which one goes first? The marble at 5.6 deg, the dice at 26.7 deg
description:
Marble or dice on a tilting tray: which one goes first? A tray 0.46 m long tilts from flat at a steady 3.00 deg/s (0.052360 rad/s) about its low edge, which stays put; a solid marble of radius 1 cm (2 cm across; I = k m R^2 with k = 2/5; the mass cancels; no rolling resistance, chosen) and a dice (a 1.6 cm cube modelled as a sliding block with grip 0.4, static equal to kinetic, a chosen number; a cube only tips above 45 degrees of tilt, so it slides first and never tips) rest side by side with their contact points 0.40 m up the tray from the edge; g = 9.807 m/s^2. In the tray frame, with x the distance up the tray from the pivot and theta = w t: the marble obeys (1 + k) x'' = -g sin(theta) + w^2 x (friction can only turn a ball, so it rolls from the first instant; closed form without the frame terms s = g (w t - sin w t) / ((1 + k) w^2)); the dice holds while g sin(theta) - w^2 x is at most mu g cos(theta) (tan(theta) = mu), then slides with x'' = -g sin(theta) + w^2 x + mu N, N = g cos(theta) + 2 w x' (the Coriolis part: a body moving toward the pivot presses less on the tray). Both integrated by RK4 at dt = 1e-04 s with a stick-slip start event, bisection for the edge arrival and a half-step rerun; after the edge each object falls freely. Shown in real time, four runs on one clock.

Measured:
- Marble: off the edge at 1.873 s, tilt 5.62 deg (5.6 on the card, six degrees narrated), speed 0.641 m/s; closed form without the frame terms 1.8707 s, 5.6121 deg; the frame terms are worth 0.0058 deg; grip needed at the edge k / (1 + k) tan(theta) = 0.0281 (any grip above that rolls it without slipping); floor push 0.9883 of its weight; spin at the edge 64.1 rad/s = 10.2 turns per second.
- Dice: holds until tan(theta) = 0.4, 21.80 deg at 7.267 s; slides and leaves at 8.891 s, 26.67 deg (26.7 on the card, twenty seven narrated), 0.744 m/s; its floor push never drops below 0.8856 of its weight.
- Margin: the dice leaves 7.02 s and 21.06 deg after the marble; when the dice starts to slide the marble has been gone for 5.40 s.
- Energy per kilogram for the marble at the edge: the tray does the work (0.2878 J/kg through its normal force); kinetic energy 0.2881 J/kg = translation 0.2058 (5/7) + spin 0.0823 (2/7); its contact point starts and ends at the pivot's height, lifted to a peak of 1.85 cm on the way.
- Other grips for the dice: 0.2 slides from 11.31 deg and leaves at 16.28 deg (5.43 s); 0.3 from 16.70, off at 21.63 deg (7.21 s); 0.5 from 26.57, off at 31.37 deg (10.46 s); 0.6 from 30.96, off at 35.70 deg (11.90 s).
- Other tilt rates, marble against dice: 1 deg/s 2.70 against 24.15 deg; 2 deg/s 4.29 against 25.52 deg; 5 deg/s 7.91 against 28.64 deg.
- Other rolling shapes at 3 deg/s: an ice cube on ice (no grip, slides) 5.02 deg; a solid cylinder 5.75; a hollow ball 5.95; a ring 6.33 deg. A 5 mm or a 20 mm marble: unchanged, the radius does not enter.
- Checks: the marble's RK4 agrees with the closed form within 2.5e-14 s and with a half-step rerun within 2.2e-15 s; the dice's half-step rerun agrees within 7.1e-15 s; 29 checks against the planning numbers, 9 failed, all nine on the dice: the planning script carried the Coriolis term in the normal force with the opposite sign (N increased instead of reduced), which puts the dice off at 8.9095 s and 26.7286 deg; the sim reproduces those numbers under that sign (13 of 13) and uses the physical sign.

Why: friction can hold a block still, but on a ball it can only make it turn, so the marble rolls as soon as the tray moves and is over the edge while the tray still looks almost flat. The block waits until the slope beats its grip, tan(theta) = 0.4 at 21.8 degrees, and only then slides; it reaches the edge at 26.7 degrees, 7 seconds after the marble. A heavier marble or dice changes nothing: the mass cancels in both.

Rerun sims/tray/tray.py with projects/tray/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
